To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nitroderivatives NO2HT, nitrohydroxy-tyrosyl acetates, and ethyl nitroroxytyrosyl ether are absorbed and metabolized in the intestine and liver.

the nitroderivatives NO2HT, N2HT-A, or NO2HT-E are well absorbed across the Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cell monolayer model, and they are extensively metabolized in the liver by glucuronidation, methylation, or both.
nitroderivatives from the olive tree phenol hydroxytyrosyl are efficiently absorbed by intestinal cells and are further extensively metabolized in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the absorption and metabolism in human cell models of the nitrocatecholic compounds NO2HT, a natural product, and its two synthetic derivatives, NO2HT-E and NO2HT-A.
the evaluation of the bioavailability and metabolism of nitrocatecholic compounds in vitro using Caco-2 (as an intestinal model) and HepG2 human cell models (as a liver model).
the development of new drugs based on the nitro derivatives of the natural compound hydroxytyrosyl.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in vitro bioavailability of nitrohydroxyphenolic compounds is high, but their bioavailability in vivo may be lower due to the high metabolic activity of these compounds in the liver.
the nitrohydroxy tyrosol derivatives are efficiently transferred across human intestinal epithelium and are extensively metabolised by hepatic cells, being NO2HT-A the most efficient compound.
NO2HT and its derivatives NO2HT-A (the most absorbed compound) and NO2HTE are bioavailable and can reach the systemic circulation, being available for further metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nitroderivatives are more bioavailable than the parent hydroxytyrosols and are extensively metabolised by hepatic cells.
nitroderivatives from HT are promising candidates as nutraceuticals and/or functional ingredients for food supplements.
nitrocatechsols are good candidates to be tested in vivo for their putative neuroprotective effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nitroderivatives studied here are bioavailable in the intestine and are extensively metabolised in the liver.
NO2HT, a nitrocatecholic derivative of HT, is a promising candidate for the prevention and/or treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, such as Parkinson's disease.
the nitration of hydroxytyrsol increases its intestinal absorption rate and the formation of methylated derivatives, which are the most abundant metabolites in the liver.
